doc.title: Branford Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Radio, acting and playing outside jazz
title: Playing with Crosby, Stills and Nash, James Taylor and Bruce Hornsby
summary: They hired him because he would not upstage the song, and he enjoyed their stories of hearing Trane.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans

blocks.x: Speaking about The Eagles, you…I remember hearing a clip where you were talking about playing with Crosby, Stills and Nash and how so many folks at that time, in their generation, the sixties, were listening to Trane. If you can talk about working with some of those non-jazz contexts.
I mean, I knew how to do it. It was fun. It was fun.
In the relationship, is there a big difference working in that context, versus working in the jazz context?
Working with the people? Talking about people, people interaction, rather than the music itself? The way people interact….

Well, they were all rich. And they were cool as hell. They were just cool. And they liked the way I played and they brought me in because of that. I think that, because of my work with Sting, they knew that I was not going to try to upstage the song. I was going to play what the song required. [And…] It was cool to hang out with them. [You know…] They told their stories about hearing Trane’s band. James Taylor…I just had a thing…. Like, his music, I love his music. And I know exactly what is required to make that music work. So, he’d just get me on these solos to do the stuff and….
You’re living in Carolina now. That’s where he…he always identified with Carolina.
Well, he’s from here, but he lives in New York. [And a…] You know, I dig doing that stuff. I dig doing it. Playing with Hornsby. It was great.

Jack DeJonnette talks about playing with Hornsby. Well that’s another thing. It’s that interpersonal relationship. I mean, you know, coming from different worlds, but there is still some common ground.
